advisory.description: Ech0 versions before 4.7.3 expose guest commenter email addresses through public API endpoints due to improper JSON serialization tags on the Comment model. Unauthenticated attackers can harvest all commenter emails by calling the /api/comments and /api/comments/public endpoints without authentication.

cwes.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

same_repository_prior_hits.mechanism: RequireScopes short-circuits with ctx.Next() whenever the JWT typ is session, before any scope or audience check. POST /login issues session tokens, so any authenticated non-admin satisfies JWTAuth/RequireAuth and then skips the only admin gate on routes that attach RequireScopes(admin:user|admin:settings) without a handler/service IsAdmin check. That lets a logged-in non-admin read GET /api/users (emails and admin flags), GET /api/system/logs, GET /api/system/visitor-stats, GET /api/system/check-update, and SSE /api/system/logs/stream. /ws/system/logs is registered on WSRouterGroup with no middleware; the handler only jwtUtil.ParseToken's the query token and never checks IsAdmin, scope, or audience, so the same session JWT tails live system logs.

Ech0's scoped access tokens promised least privilege but privileged authorization was split among JWT authentication, opt-in RequireScopes route middleware, and service-level checks of the underlying account's IsAdmin bit. A deliberately narrow admin access token, such as echo:read, therefore authenticated to privileged routes that omitted RequireScopes, including /api/inbox and panel-comment routes. The public /api/backup/export path additionally reparsed a query JWT and rebuilt viewer state from only claims.Userid, discarding token type, scopes, audience, and JTI, so the backup service saw an unrestricted admin identity and returned the database/log ZIP.

same_repository_prior_hits.mechanism: An admin-issued access JWT carrying only an unrelated minimal scope such as echo:read passed JWTAuthMiddleware and reached all nine /api/panel/comments routes because those AuthRouterGroup registrations lacked RequireScopes. The comment service then checked only the database user's admin/owner role, not the access token's scopes, allowing the limited token to read comments and settings, moderate or delete comments, change comment settings, and send test email.

same_repository_prior_hits.mechanism: A scoped access token carrying only profile:read is accepted by PUT /user because that mutating route is guarded by RequireScopes(ScopeProfileRead). UpdateUser uses the token viewer's administrator identity and permits a supplied password to replace that administrator's password. The attacker can then log in with the replacement password; login issues a session JWT, and RequireScopes deliberately bypasses scope checks for session tokens, yielding unrestricted administrator access.

same_repository_prior_hits.mechanism: GHSA-hm2h-wwwh-g49x: PUT /user (UpdateUser, can change admin password/email) is protected only by middleware.RequireScopes(authModel.ScopeProfileRead); the read-only profile:read scope is attached to a write operation, so a scoped access token issued for profile:read can change the admin password and escalate to an unrestricted session
